proposals.title: Reject a class declaring BootstrapMethods more than once
proposals.plainSummary: A class file is only allowed one BootstrapMethods attribute. We currently read the first one and ignore any others.
proposals.userBenefit: A hand-built or corrupted class file that carries two bootstrap tables is reported as broken instead of being silently read using whichever table came first.
proposals.why: JVMS 4.7.23 says at most one BootstrapMethods attribute may appear in the attributes table of a ClassFile. bootstrap_method_indices_resolve uses find_map, which takes the first and never looks for a second, so the index is bounded against a table that may not be the only one.
proposals.tradeoff: Another parse-time rejection of files that currently load, in a shape no compiler emits — so the benefit is narrow and the risk of surprising a real user is correspondingly small. It also needs a fixture the generator cannot currently build, since the attribute list is assembled per fixture.

proposals.title: Bound the static-argument indices of each bootstrap method
proposals.plainSummary: Each bootstrap method carries a list of constant pool indices for its arguments. Nothing checks those point at real pool entries.
proposals.userBenefit: The same honesty this round bought for the bootstrap method index, applied to its arguments: a file naming an argument that does not exist is broken, not unsupported.
proposals.why: BootstrapMethod.arguments is deliberately kept as raw u16 indices (see the doc comment in attribute.rs) because resolving them would turn every lambda-carrying class from unsupported back into corrupt. Bounding them is not resolving them: checking that an index is present in the pool costs nothing semantic and closes the same class of lie.
proposals.tradeoff: Must not drift into resolution. The attribute.rs comment explains at length why resolving is a regression; a bounds check has to stay a bounds check, and a future reader may not see the difference.
